title: Budget contract vocabulary
description: Objective: define the dependency-free scheduler-local budget vocabulary and hostile-input boundary required by design section 11 without granting mutation authority. Deliverable: packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-contract.ts, its one-line .js bridge, and focused contract tests covering frozen account states, buckets, reserve purposes, measurement coverage/sources, immutable record/result shapes, safe nonnegative integer/ref/version validation, and deterministic local issue ordering. NOT in scope: allocating accounts, reserving work, settling usage, policy evaluation, runtime-error mapping, persistence, or package-root export. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry and Policy approval core are DONE; copy only documented string-identical truth/policy vocabulary because @moe/scheduler intentionally has no @moe/core dependency. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-contract.ts, budget-contract.js, budget-contract.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-contract.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: Frozen account-state, bucket, reserve-purpose, measurement-coverage, measurement-source, and policy/truth compatibility vocabularies equal the pinned design and committed Policy contract values exercised by the focused tests.

Prototype-hostile, accessor, extra-key, negative, fractional, unsafe-integer, malformed-ref, malformed-version, and oversized-list inputs fail closed under a frozen module-local issue code with deterministic ordering.
Accepted records and nested collections are detached, deeply frozen, and repeat calls over equal bytes are deep-equal.
budget-contract.ts and budget-contract.test.ts are each at most 250 physical lines, the .js bridge is one exact re-export line, and the focused verification command exits 0.
taskRails: Internal kernel only: do not edit scheduler package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, src/index.ts, or import @moe/core/@moe/contracts.
Local stable reason spellings are implementation choices, not claims of design-pinned runtime codes; freeze them in tests and defer runtime mapping.
Production and test TypeScript files must each be <=250 physical lines; stage only the three explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Design + convention baseline (read-only). Design section 11 exact vocabulary (verified at lines 585-660; worker re-reads before typing): ACCOUNT STATES = OPEN | SETTLING | CLOSED | CLOSED_WITH_UNKNOWN_LIABILITY | OVERDRAWN (line ~591); BUCKETS = AVAILABLE | RESERVED | QUARANTINED | COMMITTED (four conserved integer buckets; conservation equation AVAILABLE + RESERVED + QUARANTINED + COMMITTED summed root+descendants exactly once — the equation itself is the LEDGER child's to enforce, this task only defines the vocabulary + record shapes); RESERVE PURPOSES = the design-587 protected set: VERIFICATION, REVIEW, ACCEPTANCE_PROCESSING, CONTINGENCY + fan-out INPUT_MATERIALIZATION, INTEGRATION (linear J1 protects the first four before any acceptance-bearing launch); MEASUREMENT COVERAGE = COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN (line ~634, UsageMeasurement); MEASUREMENT SOURCE = the closed source set the design names around UsageMeasurement/AdmissionQuote (~634-660: adapter-reported, correlated billing receipt, daemon observation — read the exact spellings and pin them; if the design leaves the set open, define the minimal scheduler-local closed set and mark it LOCAL in a comment). POLICY/TRUTH COMPATIBILITY: local STRING-IDENTICAL copies (task rail: no @moe/core or @moe/contracts imports) of the landed policy values needed for compatibility typing — POLICY_OUTCOMES ALLOW|DENY|REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL|HOLD_UNKNOWN and tiers R0-R3 (packages/core/src/policy/policy-contract.ts:17-30) + the 5-string truth vocabulary — each with a divergence-risk comment naming the canonical source (dependency-kernel precedent). Conventions: local BUDGET_* issue codes + local makeIssue/sortIssues/deepFreeze clones (4th clone set, consolidation note — graph-internal's closed GraphIssueCode makes reuse impossible), '../runtime-shape.js' hostile-input helpers reused read-only, one-line .js bridge, unexported subdir (Branch-A, 4th instance), integers only (design 44: no floating-point currency/token accounting).
implementationPlan.note:
Design + convention baseline, read-only. No files created.

DESIGN VOCABULARY, read at source rather than taken from the plan's summary:
- ACCOUNT STATES (design 591, verbatim, design-pinned): OPEN | SETTLING | CLOSED | CLOSED_WITH_UNKNOWN_LIABILITY | OVERDRAWN.
- BUCKETS (design 592-597, design-pinned): AVAILABLE | RESERVED | QUARANTINED | COMMITTED, integer-valued per meter. Design 609 states the conservation equation and 607 that accounts store only DIRECT buckets with roll-ups derived — I define the quadruple shape only; the equation is the ledger child's.
- MEASUREMENT COVERAGE (design 634, design-pinned): COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE PLAN, resolved in the design's favour — the measurement SOURCE set is NOT open. The plan guessed "adapter-reported, correlated billing receipt, daemon observation" and authorised a LOCAL closed set as fallback. Design section 20.5 line 1260 (benchmark binding T-D1) pins it exactly: "Every provider adapter emits `UsageMeasurement` rows using exactly `PROVIDER_REPORTED_COMPLETE`, `PROVIDER_REPORTED_PARTIAL`, `DERIVED_LIST_PRICE`, `SUBSCRIPTION_QUOTA`, `ACTUAL_BILLED`, or `UNKNOWN`". I will ship those six spellings marked DESIGN-PINNED (1260), not the plan's guess and not a LOCAL set. Adopting the plan's wording would have created a vocabulary the adapters can never emit. Note `LIST_PRICE` at design 640 is a price-kind, not a measurement source, and is deliberately not conflated with `DERIVED_LIST_PRICE`.

LOCAL, and marked as such because the design gives prose not identifiers — RESERVE PURPOSES. Design 587 says the transaction protects "mandatory verification, eligible review, final acceptance processing, and contingency reserves", and "Fan-out additionally protects input materialization and integration". Identifiers VERIFICATION, REVIEW, ACCEPTANCE_PROCESSING, CONTINGENCY, INPUT_MATERIALIZATION, INTEGRATION are my derivation from that sentence; the module comment will say so, so QA does not read them as design-pinned.

METER is an open bounded identifier, not a closed set. Design 11.2 names attempt.count / runner.authorized_ms / verification.authorized_ms as universal meters but 11.2 also admits provider-specific meters, so closing the set would be wrong. The DoD does not require a meter vocabulary.

STRING-IDENTICAL COPIES verified by value against their canonical sources, both to be re-diffed in step 4:
- POLICY_OUTCOMES ALLOW | REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL | HOLD_UNKNOWN | DENY and tiers R0-R3, from packages/core/src/policy/policy-contract.ts:17-30.
- TRUTH CLASSES OBSERVED | AGENT_REPORTED | DAEMON_VERIFIED | HUMAN_APPROVED | UNKNOWN, canonical at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:61-63, and already copied identically at dependencies/dependency-contract.ts:87 — so this is the established precedent, not a new duplication.

CONVENTIONS confirmed by reading the code, not assumed. dependencies/dependency-contract.ts is the direct precedent (250 lines, same task shape) and supplies the local clone set: deepFreeze, compareStrings, makeIssue, sortIssues over JSON.stringify, fail, oneOf, isRef, isDigest (HEX_64), isVersion, record(), denseArray() with MAX_ITEMS ceiling before element reads. runtime-shape.js exports read and confirmed: isPlainRecord/isPlainArray (proxy-rejecting via util.types.isProxy in a fail-closed try/catch), readOwnDataProperty/readOwnArrayElement (descriptor-based, {ok:false} on accessors), hasOnlyOwnStringKeys, readPlainArrayLength, hasExactDenseArrayShape. Read order per mem:convention-scheduler-validator-invariants: schema, then key-set closure, then array ceiling, then element reads.

`mem:gotcha-scheduler-js-shims` — packages/scheduler/src/budget/ does not exist yet; the .js bridge is load-bearing (the worker_threads entrypoint smoke test resolves the literal .js), and omitting it fails neither tsc nor vitest, only that smoke test. It ships in the same commit.

ZERO-AUTHORITY rail understood: types + validators only, no allocate/reserve/settle export. Sibling subdirs admission/, authority/, dependencies/ are in flight; budget/ is new and file-disjoint from all three.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-contract.test.ts (<=250 physical lines HARD — the DoD pins both files at 250, tighter than the usual 400 escape). Cases: (1) VOCABULARY EXACTNESS: frozen tuples equal the design/policy spellings from step 1 (mechanical toStrictEqual against inline expected arrays — the DoD-1 oracle); every vocabulary Object.isFrozen; (2) RECORD VALIDATION fail-closed matrix, one stable BUDGET_* code per class with deterministic sortIssues ordering: prototype-hostile objects (proxy/accessor/__proto__ tricks via runtime-shape helpers), extra keys (closed key sets), negative / fractional / unsafe-integer meter quantities (safe nonnegative integers ONLY — design integer rule), malformed refs (empty/oversized — bounded identifier validation), malformed versions, oversized lists (bounded collection ceilings before element traversal); (3) ACCEPTED records: deeply frozen, DETACHED (mutating the input object after acceptance does not alter the accepted record — snapshot semantics), nested collections frozen, repeat calls over equal bytes deep-equal (determinism); (4) shapes covered: BudgetAccountRecord {accountId, ownerRef, parentRef|null, graphRevisionRef, version, state, perMeter direct buckets (integer quadruple)}, UsageMeasurementRecord {meter, quantity|null (null when coverage UNKNOWN — never zero), coverage, source, providerRunRef, sourceParserVersion, sequence, rawReceiptDigest (hex64), observedInterval refs}, ReserveDeclaration {purpose, meter, quantity}, result union {ok:true, record}|{ok:false, issues} — shapes are DATA + VALIDATION only, zero mutation authority (no allocate/reserve/settle functions — those are the sibling children's). Confirm RED via the task's own focused command.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD red. Created packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-contract.test.ts, 246 physical lines (first draft was 256 — over the HARD 250 cap — so the 19-line import block was compacted to 7; no case was dropped to fit).

RED CONFIRMED via the task's own focused command: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-contract.test.ts` -> exit 1, "Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests no tests" — collection fails because ./budget-contract.js does not exist yet. That is the correct red for a contract module: nothing can pass by accident.

SURFACE THE TESTS PIN (nothing else may be exported as authority): vocabularies BUDGET_ACCOUNT_STATES, BUDGET_BUCKETS, BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_COVERAGES, BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES, BUDGET_RESERVE_PURPOSES, BUDGET_POLICY_OUTCOMES, BUDGET_POLICY_RISK_TIERS, BUDGET_TRUTH_CLASSES, BUDGET_ISSUE_CODES, the MAX_BUDGET_METERS ceiling, and exactly three pure validators — validateBudgetAccount, validateUsageMeasurement, validateReserveDeclaration. No allocate/settle/commit/transfer function is imported, because none may exist; movement semantics belong to the three sibling children.

DoD-1 ORACLE is mechanical toStrictEqual against inline literals, so a drifted spelling fails rather than silently passes. The measurement-source assertion pins the six design-1260 strings; a test deliberately refuses "ADAPTER_REPORTED" so the plan's guessed vocabulary cannot creep back in.

FAIL-CLOSED MATRIX, one stable BUDGET_* code per class: proxy (util.types.isProxy path), accessor-backed property, JSON-parsed own "__proto__" key, extra key, and null -> *_MALFORMED; empty/malformed refs, negative, fractional, unsafe-integer (MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2), NaN, Infinity, unknown enum values, non-lowercase and short digests -> *_FIELD_INVALID; duplicate meters and an over-ceiling list (MAX_BUDGET_METERS + 1) -> BUDGET_METER_BUCKETS_MALFORMED.

DETERMINISTIC ORDERING is tested the only way that catches a dropped sortIssues, per mem:convention-scheduler-validator-invariants: an account invalid in BOTH version and state emits two same-code issues in accumulation order (version, then state) but must be REPORTED sorted, so the assertion requires the "state" message first. An implementation that returns emission order fails.

UNKNOWN-NEVER-ZERO is pinned as a biconditional, not a one-way check: coverage UNKNOWN with quantity 0 is refused (the exact bug design 11.3 forbids), UNKNOWN with 1200 is refused, UNKNOWN with null is accepted and asserted still null; and COMPLETE or PARTIAL with null is refused, since design 11.3 makes PARTIAL an exact lower bound. PARTIAL with a genuine 0 is accepted — a measured zero is not the same fact as an unknown.

DETACHMENT is tested as snapshot semantics rather than reference equality: after acceptance the caller mutates the meters array (push), a nested bucket object, a top-level field, and the nested observedInterval; the accepted record must be unchanged on all four. Deep freezing is asserted at record, collection, and nested-element level.

Determinism over equal bytes asserted by toStrictEqual across two independent calls.

reopenReason: Governor: first child of the Conserved budget core SPIDR split, and the one the other three depend on — it defines the vocabulary they consume. Its own dependencies are satisfied: Runtime contract registry DONE, Policy approval core landed (packages/core/src/policy tracked). Plan this before Hierarchical budget ledger, Protected budget reservations, or Budget settlement reconciliation; those should declare a hard dependency on it rather than inventing their own types.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The governor authored this child directly from my earlier block analysis — scope, owned paths, rails, and the focused verification command are already exact, so no adversarial workflow was run: types-only, 3 files, every hazard class already settled by four sibling scheduler-subtree plans (local code clones because graph-internal's GraphIssueCode is closed; runtime-shape reuse; unexported subdir Branch-A; one-line bridge; string-identical local copies of policy/truth vocabularies with divergence notes because the scheduler is dependency-free by design). Alternatives rejected: (1) importing policy vocab from @moe/core — forbidden by the task rail and the package's zero-dependency invariant; (2) shipping any allocate/reserve/settle helper — the three sibling children own mutation semantics, this task grants ZERO movement authority; (3) modeling the conservation equation here — ledger child's deliverable; the vocabulary only defines the bucket quadruple shape.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Design 11 (lines 585-660) verified: account states OPEN|SETTLING|CLOSED|CLOSED_WITH_UNKNOWN_LIABILITY|OVERDRAWN; buckets AVAILABLE|RESERVED|QUARANTINED|COMMITTED (integer, conserved); protected reserve purposes per 587 (verification, review, acceptance processing, contingency; fan-out adds input materialization, integration); UsageMeasurement fields per ~634 (meter, integer quantity when known, coverage COMPLETE|PARTIAL|UNKNOWN, source, provider run ID, source/parser version, sequence, raw receipt digest, observed interval); integers throughout — no floating currency/tokens. Landed policy surface to mirror: POLICY_OUTCOMES + R0-R3 at packages/core/src/policy/policy-contract.ts:17-30. Scheduler subtree conventions established across dependencies/authority/admission plans; this is clone-set 4 with the standing consolidation note. UNKNOWN-never-zero encoded as quantity:null under UNKNOWN coverage.

(2) Measurement-source spellings: if the design leaves the set open, the LOCAL marking must be explicit or QA reads it as a design claim. (3) Vocabulary drift vs policy/truth canon — by-value diff in the adversarial step. (4) Zero-authority rail — any movement-named export is a reject.
